title: Experiment Tracking
interviewAnswer: Track code version, data version, hyperparameters, environment, metrics and artifacts so experiments can be reproduced and compared. A checkpoint without its context is not a reproducible experiment.
why: Experiment tracking makes model development reproducible and comparable instead of relying on notebook memory.
intuition: Every run should record what code/data/config produced which metrics and artifacts so you can reproduce a result and compare changes fairly.
deepDive: Track parameters/hyperparameters, code commit, data/version/split, environment, metrics over time, artifacts/checkpoints and notes. A run tracker is not the same as a model registry: tracking documents experiments; the registry governs candidate/approved model versions. Avoid logging secrets or huge raw datasets directly.
workedExample: Two diffusion runs with the same architecture but different bottleneck size should be comparable by config, seed/data version, PSNR/domain metrics, checkpoint and GPU/runtime metadata.
commonMistakes: Comparing runs trained on different data splits without noting it.
Treating experiment names as sufficient versioning.
followUps: How do you reproduce a run?
production: Link approved model versions back to their exact training runs and artifacts; this supports audits, rollback and post-incident analysis.
